report.source_text: While ileostomy was being performed, no transition zone was visualized. After surgical intervention, within 14 days, fever completely abated, and over 4 weeks significant weight gain (2 kg) was observed, both of which were a clear indications of clinical improvement.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 2-day-old Caucasian female presented with distal intestinal obstruction manifesting as reverse peristalsis, abdominal distention, fever, and inability to pass stools without stimulation. Initial rectal examination revealed no explosive gas/fluid release and an empty rectal vault (E002). Contrast enema performed on day 4 of hospitalization demonstrated absence of a transition zone (E003), suggesting long-segment or total colonic aganglionosis rather than classic Hirschsprung's disease. Approximately one month later, plain radiography revealed extensive colonic and intestinal flatulence (E004), indicating persistent obstruction. On day 75, surgical intervention was performed during which no transition zone was visualized intraoperatively (E010). Full-thickness biopsy specimens obtained from the rectum and colon during this procedure confirmed total colonic aganglionosis via pathologic examination (E008). Ileostomy was performed as definitive management, resulting in resolution of fever within 14 days and significant weight gain (2 kg) over 4 weeks postoperatively (E010).
